messages:
Ari: quick sync: I'm running a focused canary exercising handoff under churn. looking for any unexpected invariants to surface.
Priya: nice. what failures are we injecting?
Ari: owner crash, packet loss, and delayed apply acks. mix of hot prefixes + cold tenants.
Sam: main worry i have is double-commit: two nodes both think they successfully applied a takeover and both charge eviction credits. we've seen billing noise when transitions aren't strictly serialized.
Len: sounds like we should atomically CAS-pack the lease state (epoch|owner|nonce) so an apply is a single atomic op. if CAS succeeds only the committer debits credits.
Maya: agree. also recommend keeping preclaim as a cheap reservation that doesn't affect billing. only on CAS success we move to committed state and charge. avoids refunds.
Priya: what about too many outstanding preclaims? could starve global eviction capacity if nodes keep piling soft reservations.
Ari: propose soft-reserve caps per node/shard (e.g. 6), enforced by rebalancer. if exceeded, rebalancer stalls new preclaims until some finish. emit metrics for observability.
Sam: ordering: need monotonic nonces per node and pack them into CAS so newer takeovers always compare greater. avoid clock-based ordering for correctness.
Len: implementation sketch: packed_state = (epoch<<56) | (owner_id<<32) | nonce; CAS on 96-bit field (or two words) depending on arch. provide helper pack/unpack apis.
Maya: telemetry plan: counters ownership_transition_total{result=success|conflict|timeout}, gauge soft_reserve_count{node,shard}, histogram preclaim_latency_seconds, and sample traces with takeover_id tag.
Priya: read/write routing: during a pending takeover reads may still be served by the old owner for TTL window but marked stale. writes must route to sequencer which consults packed_state and either accept or forward. small perf overhead acceptable during takeover.
Ari: to reduce write overhead, cache packed_state in memory with short TTL and RCU semantics. sequencer checks cache and falls back to authoritative read only when mismatch.
Sam: tests: unit test CAS semantics under concurrency; property test ensuring only one commit per takeover_id; billing integration test ensuring commit-on-success only.
Len: docs: add section in ownership.md describing packed format, invariants (no double commit, commit-on-confirm), and failure diagrams for partition and delayed ack.
Maya: alerts: fire if ownership_conflicts > 5/min or soft_reserve_count_per_node > 4 for >1m. ops-bot: will create rules.
ops-bot: canary started on shard s-33 at 2024-09-04T11:05. watch /metrics/kv/ownership and /traces/service=kv_handshake
Priya: edge case: what if CAS succeeds on two nodes due to stale expected pack? should be impossible if we pack epoch and nonce but add defensive check to reject duplicate commits on apply RPC idempotency.
Sam: also ensure sequencer enforces single-writer invariant by tying writes to current packed owner. reject writes that don't match packed owner.
Ari: owners: I'll implement soft-reserve + packed CAS + cache; Sam will add tests; Len docs; Maya metrics/alerts. timeline: feature branches by Tue, PRs midweek.
Priya: sounds good. please tag the team in PR and include short test run logs in the PR.
Ari: will do. ping if you see weird metrics. thanks everyone :rocket:
